context: Create docs/operations/release-gates.md following the structure of docs/operations/hosted-credentials.md. Define the trigger precisely: any release whose diff touches src/todo_db/backends.py credential resolution, the wrapper template, the auth contract, or the credential documentation. Define the two required gates, the evidence each must produce in the release PR body, and the explicit statement that green CI, passing unit tests, isolated package smoke tests, and checksum verification do not satisfy them. Record the ordering rule that the downstream consumer check happens before the tag, not after, and that a failed gate blocks the tag rather than opening a follow-up. Reference scripts/hosted_auth_acceptance.sh --require by name so the gate has a runnable command, and link the page from the README release section and the CHANGELOG process notes.
description: v0.4.2 was tagged, released, and pushed into a downstream consumer before anyone executed the changed authentication path once. The readiness answer was a list of merged PRs, green CI, clean artifacts, and verified checksums, and every one of those was true while the release was unusable. This item writes docs/operations/release-gates.md, which states that artifact correctness is not evidence of usability and makes two checks mandatory before tagging any release that touches authentication, credential resolution, or the wrapper contract: the scrubbed-environment acceptance harness under --require, and one real downstream consumer running one real tracker command against the hosted database. It documents a human gate; it does not try to automate the downstream upgrade.

anti_patterns.dont: Accept green CI, passing tests, or verified checksums as evidence that a release is usable
anti_patterns.instead: require an executed hosted acceptance run and one real downstream command
anti_patterns.why: all of those passed for v0.4.2 while the released behaviour was broken for every interactive caller

anti_patterns.dont: Automate the gate by giving CI a hosted read-write credential
anti_patterns.instead: keep it a local operator step with recorded evidence
anti_patterns.why: an ambient CI write credential contradicts ADR 0004 and would mask the scrubbed-environment condition the harness tests

anti_patterns.dont: Record a failed gate as a follow-up item and tag anyway
anti_patterns.why: a gate that can be deferred at the moment it fires is not a gate

anti_patterns.dont: Run the downstream consumer check after tagging as a confirmation step
anti_patterns.instead: run it before the tag so a failure blocks the release
anti_patterns.why: v0.4.2 dispatched the downstream upgrade after publication, so the defect reached the consumer first

preserves.behavior: No credential value, hosted URL, or consumer secret is recorded as gate evidence.
Releases that do not touch authentication, credential resolution, or the wrapper contract are not subject to the downstream consumer gate.
The existing release process, versioning scheme, and artifact publication remain unchanged; this item adds gates rather than replacing steps.
The gate is a documented human check and does not add a CI job that would need hosted write credentials.
